body:
## Verification: **pass**

Built (`npm ci && npm run build`) and ran the production server (`npm run start -- --port 3000`) from a shell sourcing `.factory/sandbox/.runtime.env`, then exercised the app in Chromium and over HTTP. Evidence in `/tmp/gh-aw/agent/bsf/media/`.

| \# | Check | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | INV-1002 shows `Overdue` in its Status cell | pass |
| 2 | INV-1001 / INV-1003 (`paid`, both >30d old) show no marker | pass |
| 3 | INV-1004 (`draft`) / INV-1005 (`void`) show no marker | pass |
| 4 | `/invoices/export` body unchanged, no `Overdue` | pass |
| 5 | Button still reads `Export 3 invoices as CSV` | pass |
| 6 | `npm run build` lists `/invoices` with `ƒ` | pass |
| 7 | `npm test` green, incl. the 30/31-day boundary | pass |

### What I observed

**Checks 1–3** — browser at (localhost/redacted) (server date 2026-11-21). The accessibility snapshot reads the Status cells as `paid`, `sent Overdue`, `paid`, `draft`, `void` for INV-1001...1005 — the marker is on the one `sent` invoice and nowhere else, and the two paid invoices older than 30 days (INV-1001 at 50 days, INV-1003 at 33 days) are correctly left alone. The marker renders in red next to the status, inside the same cell, with a leading space so it does not run into the status word for a screen reader. Only console entry on the page is the pre-existing `favicon.ico` 404. Artifacts: `checks1-3-invoices-table.png`, `checks1-3-page-snapshot.yml`, `checks1-3-console.log`, and `before-invoices-table.png` (same page built from `HEAD~1`, no marker) for comparison.

**Checks 4–5** — ` curl -i (localhost/redacted) returns 200,  `text/csv; charset=utf-8` ,  `attachment; filename="invoices.csv"` ,  `no-store` , header  `id,customer,amount,issued\_on,status`  and exactly three rows (INV-1001/1002/1003);  `grep -ci overdue`  on the body is 0 and the file is 4 lines. Clicking the button in the browser downloads  `invoices-2026-11-21.csv`  with identical contents. Button label is exactly  `Export 3 invoices as CSV` . Artifacts:  `check4-export-response.txt` ,  `check4-downloaded-export.csv\`.

**Check 6** — the route table prints `ƒ /invoices` under `ƒ (Dynamic) server-rendered on demand`; the same build at `HEAD~1` prints `○ /invoices`. Corroborated beyond the marker: `/invoices` is absent from `.next/prerender-manifest.json` (`routes` holds only `/` and `/_not-found`), there is no `.next/server/app/invoices.html`, and the page responds with `Cache-Control: private, no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate`. Artifacts: `check6-build-route-table.txt`, `check6-build-route-table-BEFORE.txt`, `invoices-headers.txt`.

**Check 7** — `npm test`: 4 files, 31 tests, all passing. `lib/invoices.test.ts` includes the boundary pair — `sent` issued 2026-10-22 (exactly 30 days before `today`) is **not** overdue, 2026-10-21 (31 days) **is** — plus 29-day, paid, draft and void negatives. Artifact: `check7-npm-test.txt`.

### Ways I tried to break it

- **Reload and second click.** Reloaded the page and clicked Export twice more: both downloads are byte-identical to the first, and the marker is unchanged.
- **A different route into the same screen.** Client-side navigation from `/` to `/invoices` (Next router, not a fresh document load) renders the same `sent Overdue` cell — the marker is not a first-paint-only artefact. Artifact: `client-nav-page-snapshot.yml`.
- **Status vs. age.** INV-1003 (`paid`, 33 days) is the useful negative: a predicate that forgot the status guard would flag it. It is not flagged.
- **Frozen-at-build.** Beyond the `ƒ` marker, the per-request stack frames in `server-clockshift.log` show `isOverdue`’s `Date.parse` running inside the page render on every request against an already-built artefact, so the flag is recomputed rather than baked in.

### Notes, not failures

- I attempted a stronger end-to-end proof of the recompute by starting a second server under a `--require` shim that shifted the process clock back to 2026-10-20 (where INV-1002 is only 9 days old and should lose its marker). That server returned 500 with `TypeError: Date.parse is not a function` — the shim collides with Next’s own `node-environment-extensions/date.js`, which re-wraps the global `Date`. **This is a defect in my instrument, not in the app**: the un-shimmed server on port 3000 serves the page cleanly throughout. I fell back to the manifest/prerender/header evidence above. Both extra servers and the temporary `HEAD~1` worktree have been torn down.
- The working tree carries one uncommitted change that is not part of this commit and not in the spec’s file list: `.gitignore` gains `.playwright-cli/`. Harmless, but it is unstaged rather than committed, so flagging it rather than acting on it.
